solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Delicate matters inflamed idlers

parts.note: something inflamed is hot and burning
couch potatoes are idlers who lounge about, so idlers can be potatoes

explanation.surface: Touchy subjects have stirred up a crowd of loafers.
explanation.definitionFit: Controversial issues too awkward to handle are idiomatically called by this phrase, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Old pound is unfolded

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: An old animal pound has been laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfolded is spread out and no longer closed.

clue.text: Papa got stuck into rich spread of fish, say

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
getting stuck into food means eating it heartily, so ate

explanation.surface: Dad tucking into a rich fish paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got stuck into' is British slang for tucking in enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth paste of fish or meat spread on toast is a rich spread, fish being one example.

clue.text: Insignificant six in case

indicators.note: in means the six numeral sits inside the case word

parts.note: a legal case is a trial
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that six in a court case is trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unimportant or of little consequence is petty, minor and insignificant.

clue.text: First of these canvass for Labour

indicators.note: First of takes only the opening letter of the word these

parts.note: to canvass opinion is to ask for it

explanation.surface: An election canvassing campaign for the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it means work.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work or a job to be done is labour, a chore or duty.

clue.text: English learnt haphazardly is never-ending

indicators.note: haphazardly means randomly arranged, so the letters of learnt are mixed

explanation.surface: English picked up in a slapdash way goes on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for ever without end, everlasting, perpetual.

clue.text: New CIA offices accommodating upper-class operative

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside, here the upper-class letter
New means a fresh arrangement of the letters of CIA offices

parts.note: U is the standard label for upper-class

explanation.surface: Fresh CIA offices housing a posh secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operative' reads as a spy, given the CIA, but is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effective or working as intended is operative: producing the desired result.

clue.text: Force person in control to meet graduate — had success about that

parts.note: to police an area is to control it

indicators.note: about means the won word goes round the graduate

parts.note: someone who won had success
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A person in charge meeting a graduate, having done well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is the police force. 'in' and 'to meet' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A female officer is a member of the police force, i.e. a person in that force.

clue.text: Do avoid peripheral parts of seafront

indicators.note: avoiding the peripheral parts means dropping the two letters at each edge of seafront

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep away from the edges of the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a hairdo here, not a verb. 'avoid peripheral parts of' strips SE and NT from SEAFRONT.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a hairstyle, and this one is a rounded, bushy style of naturally curly hair.

clue.text: School with church by East Street

indicators.note: by means next to, so the church sits beside the East Street letters

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
a minster is a large church, originally one attached to a monastery

explanation.surface: Directions to a school next to a church on East Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster School is a famous public school in London, beside Westminster Abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster is the name of a celebrated independent school in central London.

clue.text: Item of dress half of clergy discarded

indicators.note: half of keeps only the front portion of the clergy word, its first four letters
discarded says the other portion of the clergy word is thrown away

parts.note: the ministry is the body of clergy collectively

explanation.surface: A garment that half the priesthood has thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' with 'discarded' keeps the front half of MINISTRY, the back half STRY being thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a short skirt or dress, so it counts as an item of clothing.

clue.text: Rely on a constant number to access this?

definitions.text: Rely on a constant number to access this?

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
c is the physics constant for the speed of light
to number things is to count them

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a fixed number will unlock something.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: the wordplay is in the first four words, and the whole clue hints at the number needed for access.
explanation.definitionFit: Money held with a bank is reached using an assigned number, hence the clue as a whole.

clue.text: Spot on! Queen recast nation's figurehead

parts.note: pat means exactly right, spot on
R is Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: recast means formed again into a new shape, so the letters of nation's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a monarch remaking a country's symbolic leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A nation's figurehead is its protective saint, like St George for England.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian saint of a country serves as its emblematic figurehead.

clue.text: Reorganise a horse pound

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
to pound something is to ram or batter it

explanation.surface: An order to rearrange a horse enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like an animal pen, but it is the verb meaning batter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange letters into a new word is to treat them as a word puzzle of this kind, used as a verb.

clue.text: 'Right,' Mike said, …

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something said is spoken, oral

explanation.surface: Mike speaks, beginning a quote that runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical and righteous, so right in the sense of good conduct.

clue.text: Give the green light to rendezvous with bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a man, in British slang
a rendezvous is an arranged meeting, a date

explanation.surface: Approving a romantic meeting with some fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise or officially require something is to give permission for it, i.e. approve it.

clue.text: '… being in charge is ludicrously busy'

parts.note: a being is a creature or person, such as a man

explanation.surface: Mike's remark continued: being the boss is crazily hectic.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantically or wildly energetic and frenzied, so absurdly busy.

clue.text: Left to make new opening for said watering hole

indicators.note: a new opening means the first letter of the said word is swapped for another

parts.note: said aloud means spoken, which is vocal

explanation.surface: Someone instructed to cut a new entrance into a drinking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make new opening for' replaces the V of VOCAL with L.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the nearest pub is called this, and a pub is a watering hole in slang.

clue.text: Stop turning round to avoid a trip hazard?

indicators.note: to avoid means leave out, so the letter a is dropped
turning round signals the stop word read backwards

parts.note: a break is a stop or pause

explanation.surface: A stop sign telling you to turn back and avoid something that might make you stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning round' gives KAERB; 'to avoid a' then drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised edge of a pavement is something pedestrians can catch a foot on, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mediterranean dough — stop if nothing goes right

indicators.note: going right means moving along to the right-hand end of the word

parts.note: to foil a plan is to stop or thwart it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A recipe warning about pastry: stop if nothing turns out well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests money, but it is pastry. In FOIL the O 'goes right', moving to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This paper-thin pastry is a staple of Greek and Middle Eastern baking around the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Foundation is after graduates

indicators.note: after means the is comes behind the graduates

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, i.e. graduates

explanation.surface: A statement that a foundation follows on from graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the groundwork or underlying support on which something rests.

clue.text: Steady airline about to enter prescribed course

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: to enter means the about letter goes inside the course word

parts.note: a lane is a fixed course to keep to, as in swimming or running
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: An airline steadying itself on a set flight path.
explanation.definitionFit: To steady something is to keep it stable and in equilibrium, i.e. to poise it.

clue.text: Sarnie on the hoof packed with last of tinned fish

indicators.note: packed with means the anagram has something stuffed inside
on the hoof means on the move, so the letters of Sarnie move about
last of takes the final letter of tinned

explanation.surface: A sandwich eaten on the go, stuffed with tinned fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish often sold tinned is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Major unit of currency — bar won't accept one

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of many currencies

indicators.note: refusing to accept something means it is kept out of the bar word

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as in a towel rail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pub refusing to take a big unit of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' reads as describing the currency, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something principal or chief is at the centre of things, so main and major.

clue.text: Break a saucer in pieces

indicators.note: a saucer in pieces is smashed, so its letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Smashing a saucer into fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or division in a line of verse is a break in its rhythm.

clue.text: Sports stadium back where one goes over?

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: back means the lavatory word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lav (lavatory) is where one goes, euphemistically

explanation.surface: A quip about stadium toilets at the back, where people pop off during the game.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in south London is a well-known cricket ground, i.e. a sports venue.

clue.text: Manifest slope

definitions.meaning: a manifest is a ... of cargo or passengers
a ship that leans to one side has a lean or tilt

explanation.definitionFit: A cargo manifest is an inventory, and a tilt to one side is a lean, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Who managed India?

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, so managed is ran
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A history quiz question about who governed India.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-all-in-one: the whole clue defines, with 'managed India' as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu queen or a rajah's wife who ruled a state, so one who governed part of India.

clue.text: Connect with this writer beginning to study hard

parts.note: this writer is the setter, i.e. me

indicators.note: beginning to takes just the first letter of study

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The setter linking up with someone to start studying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that engage interlock, so to engage or fit together is to connect.

clue.text: EU admitting faults for disaster of this sort?

indicators.note: faults suggests errors or breaks, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: The European Union owning up to mistakes that caused a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'an unmitigated disaster' means a complete, total one, so this word describes such a disaster.

clue.text: So many Muses over the moon being on this cloud

definitions.meaning: Greek myth counts the Muses as a set of this many sisters

definitions.text: over the moon being on this cloud
definitions.meaning: being on cloud ... is an idiom for being over the moon, i.e. elated

explanation.definitionFit: The Muses numbered nine, and on cloud nine is the idiom for elation, both fitting the number.

clue.text: Rise with dawn? Have an epiphany

parts.note: to seethe is to surge or rise up, like boiling water
first light is dawn, so light can stand for daybreak

explanation.surface: Getting up at daybreak and having a sudden revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests watching the sunrise, but 'Rise' is the bubbling-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for suddenly understanding something, which is what a sudden insight or revelation is.
